title: The Catalyst for the July Revolution

entries.title: Background
entries.content: In 2018, student protests led the Bangladesh government to abolish the existing quota system for government jobs. In June 2024, the High Court reinstated a 30 percent quota reserved for descendants of freedom fighters, ruling the 2018 circular that had abolished it illegal. Students organising under the banner Anti-Discrimination Student Movement raised a four-point demand, including cancelling the reinstatement and ensuring merit-based recruitment. Separately, teachers at 35 public universities were already on strike over changes to their pension scheme, suspending academic and administrative activities — a parallel dispute running alongside the student movement.

entries.title: What Followed
entries.content: Most student protests began on 1 July 2024 at public university campuses, including Dhaka University, and were peaceful at this stage. On 4 July 2024, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court upheld the High Court's ruling, after which protests intensified. In the weeks that followed, the movement grew and, from mid-July onward, was met with a violent crackdown — a period covered in later chapters.
